$comment: Doodles art data. Lengths are in units of a 400 x 400 artboard (multiply by artboard short side / 400), or given as percentages. Colours are roles only; hex values always come from the product's Wada combination. Numbers are rules of thumb tuned on sample.mjs and the references in research.md, unless a source is given.

line.$comment: One pen per piece: a fineliner for walls and pages, a marker for margin pieces with a big focal object. Never both.

fineliner.use: Wall and page modes, small marks (most marks 20-45 units across).

marker.use: Margin mode, where a focal object is 35-55% of the short side and marks are larger.

line.wobbleVsHumanist: About twice the relative wobble of Humanist Minimal and on a thinner line, so marks read as quick, not considered.

overshoot.$comment: Hands overshoot. Closed shapes don't close exactly; corners can run past.
overshoot.share: At least half of the closed shapes in a piece overshoot or leave a gap.

line.doublePass: Optional: one in five outlines may get a second, looser pass offset 1-2 units, as when a doodler goes over a line again. Never on text.
rules: One weight in a piece: never thicker lines for important things. Importance comes from size, fill and position.
Ink is Wada Black on light grounds, or Wada White on a Wada Black ground (chalk mode). Never grey, coloured or dashed.
Stroke width does not scale with the mark: a small star and a big star use the same pen.
Points (star tips, arrowheads, zigzags) are rounded by the round cap; no hairline spikes.

shape.$comment: Doodle shapes are outlines first. Closed shapes may take a flat fill, printed off the line.

fills.offsetDirection: One direction for the whole piece (down-right by default), as if printed in two passes.
fills.coverage: The fill is the same shape as the outline, shifted; it may fall short of or run past the line on one side.

rules: Fills are flat colour only: no hatching inside a coloured fill.
Never trace a fill exactly inside its ink line.
One accent-coloured object per piece; other fills use the support colour or Wada White.

corners.$comment: Layout and UI around the art. Doodles adds a hand-drawn frame option to the usual radius scale.

use.button: pill or md, with a solid fill and set type (never a hand-drawn button outline alone; it must look pressable)
use.card: lg, or a hand-drawn ink frame with a 2-4 unit wobble
use.image: lg, or a hand-drawn blob mask

corners.sketchFrame: A hand-drawn outline in the piece's pen around a card or photo, drawn 3-6 units outside the box, overshooting at one corner.
corners.print: On posters and print, image box corners are 2-4% of the box's short side, or a sketch frame.

modes.use: Default. A focal object or a headline, with 5-15 marks clustered around it like notes in a margin. Ads, social posts, landing heroes, packaging.
modes.placement: Marks sit within 1.5 margins of the focal element or the headline, on at most two of its sides.

modes.use: Sketchnotes: explaining a process, an agenda, a menu, a recap. Several small ideas joined into one route.
modes.placement: Clusters follow a reading path (Z, S or numbered); arrows, connectors and numbers show the order. One cluster is the focal one, at least 1.5x the others.

modes.use: All-over pattern: a brand wall, packaging wrap, event backdrop, a hero that must stop people from across a room. At most one piece in three in a campaign.
modes.gapBetweenMarks: 1-3 pen widths; no holes larger than one mark

clearing.shape: A hand-drawn cloud, blob or bubble outline in the same pen, filled with paper or ground
clearing.holds: The focal object or the headline, never both crowded in

modes.edge: The wall stops on a drawn edge (a wobbly line) or runs off the artboard; never fades.

composition.pairing: Marks and headline work together: the marks point to or react to the words; they never repeat them as pictures (W5).
rules: Choose one mode per piece and state it in the brief.
Body text, prices and calls to action sit on plain ground or paper with a mark-free band of at least one margin around them.
One focal point per piece, at least 3x the size of any other mark.
Marks point inwards, to the message: arrows and sparkles never lead the eye off the artboard.
In wall mode, the brand name and headline live in or next to the clearing, never on top of marks.

palette.$comment: Share of the visible area for each colour role, by mode. Colours come from the product's Wada combination.

ground.from: combination bg (a light colour, L* 80 or more)

ink.from: Wada Black (Wada White in chalk mode)

fill.from: One support colour of the combination

method: Start from combinations that contain a light colour (L* 80 or more) to use as ground; doodles need a pale page for black ink to read.
Black ink must reach AA (4.5:1) on the ground; every recommended combination passes at 9:1 or more (most at 12:1 or more).
Use the strongest-chroma colour of the combination as the accent (one object) and at most one other as the fill colour.
Combinations that include Wada Black can also run in chalk mode: black ground, Wada White ink, fills from the other colours. Use it for one piece in a set, not as default.
Avoid combinations whose only light colour is a muddy buff or olive for walls: large ink areas make them look dirty.

recommendedCombinations.why: Loud, primary-feeling page: Yellow ground, Carmine accent, Diamine Green fills, Black ink built in. Best for walls.
Bright notebook yellow with a warm red accent; Raw Sienna fills suit food and craft.
Soft pink page with a fresh green accent and pink fills; playful without being loud.
Kraft-paper notebook feel; one red accent. Good for margin and page modes.
Primary trio: Yellow ground, Blue fills, Carmine accent; strong sticker energy for walls.
Calm two-colour page: pale pink ground, Blue as both fill and accent. Margin mode.
Sky-blue page with deeper Blue fills; cool and clear for tech or health.
Very light lemon page with one hot accent; the quietest ground for page-mode sketchnotes.
Pale aqua page with a warm red accent: a cooler alternative for margin mode.
Ink on yellow only, or chalk mode (Yellow ink fills on a Black ground) for a single stand-out piece.
Warm peach page, orange accent, green fills: friendly for food and family products.

hatching.$comment: The only shading. Parallel pen strokes, like shading in a notebook margin.
hatching.crossHatch: A second set at 90 degrees for the darkest areas only.
hatching.use: Shadows, the dark side of an object, emphasis bands on one focal shape.

stipple.use: Sparkle, dust, crumbs, filler between wall marks.

texture.grain: None on screen. On print, a real pen or a pen texture brush is welcome.

vocabulary.$comment: Marks and what they usually do. Pick marks for their job (DD2); in wall mode, mix 6-10 kinds and repeat them.

marks.draw: Curved shaft, open two-stroke head; curly arrows for a playful route.
Loop drawn around a word or object, overshooting its start.
Wavy or double line under one word, never a whole sentence.
Five points, rounded tips; may get the accent fill.
Four or eight short strokes crossing, or 3 tick marks around an object.
Open spiral of 2-3 turns.
A short sine or zigzag line.
A line with 2-4 loop-de-loops on the way to its target.
Wobbly bubble with a tail; holds 1-6 set words.
Bumpy cloud with two or three small trailing circles.
Round outline, two dot eyes, one line mouth. No noses, no cheeks, no lashes.
Slightly lopsided, closed with an overshoot.
Two strokes, the second longer; for lists.
Hand-drawn numeral in a circle.
Almond outline with a filled pupil.
Small disc with 6-10 short rays.
Looped petals around a small centre.
Parallel strokes at 45 degrees.
Groups of 3-5 single-pen-width dots.
Simple hand with one pointing finger; use once per piece.

avoid.why: The copy rules ban them; drawn ones say the same thing.
The most worn-out symbol in advertising.
Common in real notebooks, wrong for brands; they hijack the message.
Haring's babies and dogs, Mr Doodle's characters and Burgerman's creatures are signatures of named artists and estates. Draw your own.
Belong to a living subculture with its own rules; faking them reads as costume.

avoid.symbol: emoji or icon-pack doodles used unchanged
avoid.why: Perfect, generic and seen everywhere; they break the one-pen rule.

method.$comment: How to make a doodle piece: think out loud around one message. Adapted from sketchnoting practice (research.md 2.2).
recipe: Write the one message in a sentence (W1).
Pick the mode: margin, page or wall (composition.modes). Most pieces are margin.
Draw the focal: one object from the product's world, or the hand-lettered headline itself, at the focal size for the mode.
Think out loud around it: add marks that point (arrow, circle), count (numbers, checks), celebrate (star, sparkle) or react (face, bubble). Each mark has one job.
Fill some closed shapes with the support colour, offset in one direction; give the accent to the one object that matters most.
Count and cut: stay inside the mode's mark count and empty-ground minimum. Remove any mark that does nothing.
Set the body text and call to action in clear type, with a mark-free band around them.

examples.marks: steam squiggles, a sparkle on the cup, an arrow to the price, a small smiling face
examples.idea: the first good moment of the day

examples.marks: arrows between steps, checks, one star on the last step
examples.idea: how the service works, in 30 seconds

examples.focal: a pen drawing a loop that becomes a star, in a paper cloud
examples.marks: stars, spirals, faces, clouds, hearts, squiggles all over

checklist: Mode chosen (margin, page or wall) and its counts respected.
One pen: one stroke width everywhere, round ends, visible wobble, loops overshoot.
One focal element at least 3x any other mark; in wall mode it sits in a clearing of 25-40%.
Every mark near the message has a job (point, count, celebrate, react, link).
Black ink on a light Wada ground; fills from at most two combination colours, offset in one direction; accent on one object.
Hand lettering only for the headline (up to 8 words) or short labels; body and CTA set in type, with a mark-free band around them.
No drawn exclamation marks, no copied artist characters, no stock icons.
